memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But the men inside reached out and pulled Lot back into the house and shut the door. Then they struck the men who were at the door of the house, young and old, with blindness so that they could not find the door. - Gen 19:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At the very moment the mob is about to break down the door, the angels act. They reach out, pull Lot back to safety, and strike the attackers with blindness so they grope helplessly, unable even to find the door. Lot, who had put himself in danger, is rescued by a power far greater than his own. He did not save himself; he was saved.

There is a picture of grace here. Lot was in an impossible situation, moments from disaster, powerless to protect himself. And divine hands reached out and pulled him back. Salvation, in the end, is not something we accomplish; it is something done to us and for us by God.

Notice too the mercy hidden even in the judgement on the mob. They were struck with blindness - but blindness that stopped them, that ended their assault, that spared them from completing their wickedness that night. Even God's acts of judgement often contain a restraining mercy.

This is the gospel pattern. We were helpless, unable to rescue ourselves, and God reached out and pulled us to safety. "It is by grace you have been saved... not by works, so that no one can boast" (Eph 2:8-9). Whatever danger presses against your door today, remember: the God who reached out and saved Lot reaches out still. Salvation belongs to the Lord.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you try to save yourself, or trust the God who reaches out to rescue?
- Where do you need God's saving hand to pull you to safety today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I cannot save myself. Thank You that You reach out and rescue the helpless. When danger presses against my door, pull me to safety by Your grace, for salvation belongs to You alone.
Amen.
